calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Penguins.

calls.head: Like for like: Hertl against Kindel
calls.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Hertl’s line (Hertl, Lavoie and Connelly) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Penguins’ third line is Robertson, Kuzmenko and Kindel.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Golden Knights pile it on the Penguins
paras: Rasmus Andersson and Noah Hanifin scored just under three minutes apart early in the first to put the Golden Knights up 2-0. Jérémy Lauzon and Declan Carlile squared off early in the period. Mark Stone made it 3-0 for the Golden Knights on the power play late in the period. Sidney Crosby got the Penguins on the board on the power play early in the second, and Trevor Connelly stretched the lead to 4-1 a little over a minute later. The Penguins’ Samuel Girard left in the second period and didn’t return. Shea Theodore made it 5-1 for the Golden Knights midway through the period, but Evgeni Malkin cut Vegas’ lead to 5-2 early in the third. Brett Howden added an empty-net goal with a little over two minutes left to make it 6-2. Stone finished with a goal and two assists.

The Penguins had a little more of the play. The Golden Knights had the finish. Adin Hill made 22 saves for the Golden Knights, and Sergei Murashov allowed five goals on 19 shots. The Knights moved to 8-2-0, and the Penguins fell to 3-5-1.

items.text: Mark Stone passed William Karlsson for second on the Golden Knights’ all-time scoring list, with 410 points.
